brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;half-n is the only base placed; get_build shows total counts piece:1.

requirements.requirement: Nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: No neighboring bases in any of the 6 adjacent cells and no level 1 piece; get_build total=2 (piece+drawer) and check_build meshClash clear.

Only one drawer possible per half base. After placing half-n, half-s, half-e, etc., find_sockets for drawer returns 1 offer then 0 after it is used; variants slide/swing/long and storeys 2/3 also return 0. Build has drawer:0#0,0#cut (1/5). The configurator rule prevents 5 drawers on a single cell, so requirement cannot be completed as asked.

finish.summary: Single half-n base built with one drawer as far as the configurator allows. The five-drawer requirement is unmet because the system permits at most one drawer per half base (one cut face), with zero additional offers after the first is placed across all variants checked.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
